summary: The Tavascan is Cupra's only battery-electric model in Australia, a coupe-roofed mid-size SUV on the same MEB platform as the Volkswagen ID.5 and Skoda Enyaq, now sold in three grades after the MY27 update added a 58kWh LFP entry V below the 77kWh Endurance and dual-motor VZ. Australian reviewers rate its steering and body control above most rivals and CarsGuide singles out the ride as a surprise strength, though Chasing Cars found the Endurance's firm rear suspension tiring and reviewers still criticise the 135kW DC charging peak, cabin squeaks and the lack of connected services. The update also raised the Endurance by $5,500 and lifted the VZ to $75,490, just over the $75,000 FBT cap that applies from April 2027.
pros: Sharp chassis: Chasing Cars found the Endurance 'excels' through corners with little body roll and accurate steering, and CarsGuide called the ride quality the car's biggest surprise, with the VZ's adaptive dampers giving a supple ride

The new V opens the range at $55,490 before on-road costs, about $3,400 under a Tesla Model Y RWD per Chasing Cars, with heated power front seats, Sennheiser audio, a 360-degree camera and 20-inch wheels standard
540 litres seats-up and 1,550 litres seats-down on every grade, with a low, flat boot floor and rear space CarsGuide rated ample for adults up to about 180cm
Five-year unlimited-kilometre factory warranty with no Cupra-network servicing condition stated, plus 8 years/160,000km on the high-voltage battery with a 70 per cent capacity floor

The VZ is rated to tow 1,800kg braked against 1,000kg for the V and Endurance, and adds 250kW all-wheel drive (0-100km/h in 5.5 seconds), DCC adaptive dampers, a fixed panoramic roof and matrix high beams
cons: The VZ at $75,490 sits $490 over the $75,000 FBT full-exemption cap that applies to novated leases from 1 April 2027, while the Endurance rose $5,500 to $66,490 in the MY27 update (the former $4,500 Interior Package is now standard)
Slow DC charging: 135kW peak on the 77kWh grades, which Chasing Cars called disappointing, and just 105kW on the V's 58kWh LFP pack

Chasing Cars measured 18.3kWh/100km on the Endurance, implying about 421km per charge, and CarExpert saw 19.8kWh/100km in the VZ against its 17.4kWh/100km claim; the V's 414km claim is the shortest in the range

No connected services on Australian cars as of CarExpert's January 2026 review (no app, remote preconditioning or over-the-air updates), and vehicle-to-load was still unconfirmed for the MY27 car at its June 2026 announcement
Reviewers found squeaks and some cheap cabin materials, a grainy hand-over from regen to the rear drum brakes, no spare wheel on any grade, and a four-star ANCAP rating versus five from Euro NCAP
